topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the core learning outcomes regarding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications drive clonal fitness, expansion, and Darwinian selection in cancer development.

topics.label: Stemness, cancer stem cells, and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue stem cell hierarchies, cancer stem cell models, and the cell of origin contribute to tumor initiation and progression.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how extrinsic factors such as inflammatory signals, microenvironmental promoters, and supportive stroma permit and sustain tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Technologies for investigating tumor evolution and spatial architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews the genomic, computational, and spatial omics methodologies used to analyze tumor cell interactions and mutational histories.

topics.label: Integrated multi-factorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how genetic alterations, cell-of-origin properties, and permissive microenvironments converge in an evolutionary framework to drive malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and introduces the topic of cancer therapy for the following lecture.
